items.rationale: (a) keeps the chase acting on the real stop price at the cost of a small change on the stop path; (b) leaves a stop that the app believes moved when it did not.
items.question: When Deribit refuses an edit of the triggered stop limit, the app today still records the stop at the new price it asked for, so its chase can stop re-sending while the real stop sits at the old price. What should the app do on a refused stop edit?

options.text: Reset the chase reference to the stop price from the exchange's latest echo, so the next tick re-targets from the truth (still under the existing retry backoff).
options.label: (a)

items.rationale: The owner is often away from the screen; a stop that cannot move is a protection failure even if the M.SL cap remains. (b) costs nothing but leaves the owner unaware.
items.question: A triggered stop limit whose edits keep being refused cannot follow the market; today the app only logs. The M.SL emergency flatten still works independently. Should the app page?

options.text: Urgent page once per episode after 3 consecutive refused edits of the triggered stop, or 10 s with the confirmed stop price behind the chase target.
options.label: (a)

items.rationale: An oversize, non-reduce-only take-profit can flip the account with no stop; repeated bounded retries close that window. (b) is simpler but leaves it open after one refusal.
items.question: The take-profit must equal the position; when Deribit refuses the resize edit, the once-a-second check retries only once per episode, so an oversize take-profit can stay oversize. What retry policy?

options.text: Keep retrying on the stop backoff schedule (0.67 s doubling to a 5 s cap) until the take-profit matches; one page per episode.
options.label: (a)

options.text: One retry per episode, as built.
options.label: (b)

items.rationale: (a) keeps the entry chase and its logs truthful; the entry is not a protection path, so (b) is lower risk than the stop case but still misleads the owner and the chase.
items.question: When Deribit refuses an entry-chase edit, the app still records the entry at the new price and logs it as repositioned. What should it do?

options.text: Reset the entry reference to the entry price from its latest echo and log the refusal.
options.label: (a)
